commits.message:
fix(export): a trailing blank row is drawn in the HTML export A newline straight before ends a line without drawing another, so a recording ending in a blank row lost it. Every row now ends with its own newline, matching the newline the page writes after 
 for the parser to
drop. Checked in headless Chromium: the pre's height in lines equals
exportLines' row count for blank rows first, last, both and in between.

fix(export): a double underline no longer doubles strike and overline

CSS gives an element one text-decoration-style, so underline2 sharing a span
with strike drew a double strike-through the terminal never showed. The
double underline now sits on an outer span carrying the paint (so no inner
background covers it) and the blink (so it blinks with the glyph); strike and
overline stay single on the inner span. Checked in headless Chromium over a
painted background.

feat(export)!: theme-aware, attribute-complete HTML export (rich-export-9a1.2)

Console.exportHtml({ theme?, clear? }) now draws exportLines' resolved picture
through a new core module, export-html (encodeHtml). The page's background and
default text colour come from the theme via a new exportCanvas in export-lines,
the same ground resolveLook flattens runs over. Every ExportLook field is
written: reverse and dim arrive as resolved colours (no opacity), double
underline, strike, overline, blink via keyframes, frame and encircle, and
allowed links as <a> elements. Refused links export as styled text. pre no
longer re-wraps recorded rows.

saveHtml and saveText take the full option type of the export they write.

BREAKING CHANGE: Style.getHtmlStyle is removed with no replacement; export
through Console.exportHtml. The exported HTML markup changes shape.

feat(export): shared export resolution for HTML and SVG (rich-export-9a1.1) (#150)

* feat(export): resolve recorded output into the rows both exporters draw (rich-export-9a1.1)

The research ticket asked for design/export-pipeline.md. CLAUDE.md forbids a
second description of a subsystem outside docs/, so the design lands as the
module that makes it true, with the rationale in its header and the claims
pinned by tests.

src/core/export-lines.ts resolves a recorded Segment stream under a
TerminalTheme into rows of { text, look } runs. ExportLook carries only
resolved values: reverse, dim, conceal, default colours and the theme's ANSI
table are consumed here, so neither the HTML nor the SVG exporter can forget
one. parseHref is the single checkpoint for links an export may publish
(http, https, mailto, ftp, file); a refused link keeps its text.

Nothing consumes it yet: rich-export-9a1.2 routes exportHtml through it and
deletes the two style-to-CSS converters it replaces.

* fix(export): flatten alpha before reverse, dim and conceal (rich-export-9a1.1)

resolveLook handed translucent colours straight to the swap, the fade and
conceal. toSgrCodes flattens first, so an exported #rrggbbaa run drew other
colours than the terminal did, and conceal over a translucent background left
the glyph visible. Paper now flattens over the theme canvas and ink over the
paper, through ColorSpec.flattenAlpha, before anything else sees them.
